options.text: Leo lo tengo is correct
Lo tengo que leer is the only correct form
Tengo lo que leer is correct
Tengo que leerlo attaches the pronoun to the infinitive

questions.explanation: The pronoun can attach to the infinitive: Tengo que leerlo. Placing it before the conjugated verb is also valid.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.stem: A newsroom editor asks why quien carries an accent in a question but not in a relative clause. Explain.

answer.exemplar: Interrogative quien carries an accent to mark it as a question word, while relative quien does not.

questions.explanation: The accent distinguishes interrogative from relative use. It signals question or exclamation.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Direct address and the verb form
questions.learningObjective: Use correct form for tu direct address

stimulus.body: Error comun: El rotulo dice Ustedes vayan con cuidado pero se dirige a un amigo.

questions.stem: Which form is correct for tu?

options.text: Vayan con cuidado fits tu
Ve con cuidado fits tu
Id con cuidado fits tu
Ir con cuidado fits tu

questions.explanation: Tu takes the second-person singular command: ve. The other forms are ustedes, vosotros or infinitive.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Use a phrase to soften an opinion
questions.stem: A newsroom editorial wants to soften a claim. Which phrase does that?

options.text: Sin duda softens the claim
Es un hecho que softens the claim
Me parece que softens the claim
Es evidente que softens the claim

questions.explanation: Me parece que softens the claim by marking it as personal. The other phrases assert certainty.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: Gerund and infinitive after a verb
questions.stem: A common mistake: Sigo a leer el informe. Which correction is needed?

options.text: Sigo a leyendo el informe is correct
Sigo a leer el informe is already correct
options.misconception: seguir takes gerund, not a plus infinitive

options.text: Sigo leido el informe is correct
Sigo leyendo el informe is correct

questions.explanation: Seguir plus gerund expresses continuation. A plus infinitive, participle or mixed forms are wrong.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.stem: A reporter asks how to report He dicho que he terminado. Give the shifted form.

answer.exemplar: The shifted form is Dijo que habia terminado, moving present perfect to pluperfect.

questions.explanation: Reported speech shifts present perfect to pluperfect. Habia terminado replaces he terminado.

questions.subject: SPANISH

stimulus.body: Error comun: El testigo dijo: este coche es mio. El redactor escribe Este coche es mio.

questions.stem: Which correction fixes the demonstrative?

options.text: Dijo que este coche era mio
options.misconception: demonstrative and possessive do not shift

options.text: Dijo que ese coche era suyo
Dijo que aquel coche era suyo
Dijo que ese coche era mio

questions.explanation: Reported speech shifts este to ese and mio to suyo. The other options keep one or both unshifted.
questions.hint: Shift este to ese and mio to suyo.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Report a command with tener que
questions.stem: A reporter wants to report Tienes que salir. Which form fits?

options.text: Dijo que tuvo que salir
options.misconception: preterite is not the reported form

options.text: Dijo que tienes que salir
options.misconception: second person does not shift to reported form

options.text: Dijo que tenia que salir
Dijo que tendra que salir
options.misconception: future is not the reported form

questions.explanation: Reported commands with tener que shift to imperfect: tenia que salir. The other forms keep wrong person or tense.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.topic: How far a report reaches back
questions.learningObjective: Identify a report about a habitual past
questions.stem: A newsroom report says El testigo dijo que siempre llegaba tarde. What does it convey?

options.text: An ongoing state
options.misconception: llegaba habitual is not a state

options.text: A single completed event
options.misconception: siempre signals habit, not single event

options.text: A future plan
A habitual past action reported in the past

questions.explanation: Siempre llegaba reports a habitual past action. It is not a single event, future plan or state.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Add a reporting verb to a draft
questions.stem: A newsroom draft lacks a reporting verb: La obra termino. Rewrite it as reported speech.

answer.exemplar: The reported form is El director dijo que la obra habia terminado.

questions.explanation: Adding a reporting verb and shifting the tense turns the bare fact into reported speech.

questions.subject: SPANISH
questions.learningObjective: Apply reported speech to a complex sentence

stimulus.body: Error comun: El testigo dijo: manana ire a la comisaria. El redactor escribe Dijo que manana ire a la comisaria.

questions.stem: Which correction applies all shifts?

options.text: Dijo que manana ire a la comisaria is already correct
Dijo que manana iria a la comisaria
Dijo que manana fue a la comisaria
Dijo que manana habia ido a la comisaria

questions.explanation: Reported speech shifts future to conditional: iria. The other options keep future, use preterite or pluperfect incorrectly.
